stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Tomato growers have long planted marigolds between their rows, believing that the flowers' strong scent drives away whiteflies, a common pest of tomato plants. However, in a three-year field trial, agronomist Priya Venkataraman found that tomato plants grown alongside marigolds carried just as many whiteflies as tomato plants grown with no marigolds nearby. Her results cast doubt on the idea that ______
choices: whiteflies prefer to feed on marigolds rather than on tomatoes.
marigolds planted among tomatoes help protect them from whiteflies.
whitefly numbers on tomatoes do not change when marigolds are nearby.
tomatoes grown without marigolds yield more fruit than other tomatoes.
explanation: The old view is that marigolds keep whiteflies off tomatoes. Venkataraman found the same number of whiteflies with or without marigolds, so her trial attacks exactly that belief. The blank comes after "cast doubt on the idea that," so it has to restate the old view.

A.why: The trial counted whiteflies on tomato plants only. It never tested whether whiteflies like marigolds better, so you added a claim the passage doesn't contain.

C.why: This is what the new trial supports, not what it casts doubt on. You attached the choice to the wrong side of the "however."

D.why: The trial measured whiteflies, not fruit yield. This choice shifts to a topic the passage never discusses.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Some astronomers have interpreted the reddish color of Orla, a small icy body beyond Neptune, as a sign that its surface is coated with frozen methane, which darkens and reddens when exposed to sunlight over long periods. But new infrared observations of Orla show none of the light-absorption patterns that methane ice reliably produces, casting doubt on the idea that ______
choices: Orla's surface is covered with a layer of frozen methane.
Orla's reddish color is caused by a material besides methane.
Orla does not actually appear reddish when it is observed.
all reddish bodies beyond Neptune lack methane on their surfaces.
explanation: The old interpretation is that Orla's red color comes from frozen methane on its surface. The new observations find no sign of methane ice, so they undercut that exact claim. The blank restates the view that is being doubted.

B.why: If the red color isn't from methane, it must come from something else, so the new evidence points toward this idea rather than against it. You picked the side of the "but" that the data supports.

C.why: The passage treats Orla's reddish color as a given. The new data question what causes the color, not whether the color is there.

D.why: The observations covered only Orla. Stretching one object's result to "all" reddish bodies is strength creep.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Many dietitians have advised against drinking water with meals, reasoning that the extra liquid dilutes stomach acid and therefore slows digestion. However, when nutrition researchers measured stomach acidity and digestion time in volunteers who drank water with a meal and in volunteers who did not, they found no meaningful difference between the two groups, casting doubt on the claim that ______
choices: water consumed during a meal passes through the stomach quickly.
drinking water with a meal interferes with the process of digestion.
people should avoid drinking large amounts of water at any time.
stomach acidity stays the same whether or not water is consumed.
explanation: The dietitians' view is that water with meals slows digestion by diluting stomach acid. The study found no difference in acidity or digestion time, which knocks out that reasoning. So the blank restates the old claim.

A.why: The study measured acidity and total digestion time. It didn't track how fast the water itself moves through the stomach, so this choice is about a detail nobody tested.

C.why: The passage is only about water with meals. A rule about avoiding water "at any time" goes far beyond both the old advice and the new study.

D.why: This is what the study found, so it can't be the idea the study casts doubt on. You landed on the wrong side of the "however."

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Because its outline of the coast closely matches older Portuguese charts, historians long assumed that a 1583 map by cartographer Tomás Reyna was simply copied from those earlier works. Recent analysis, however, shows that Reyna's map records water depths and several small inlets that appear on no earlier chart of the region, casting doubt on the idea that ______
choices: Reyna's map was merely copied from older Portuguese charts.
Reyna personally surveyed every inlet shown on his 1583 map.
Reyna's map includes details missing from the earlier charts.
older Portuguese charts depicted that coastline with accuracy.
explanation: The historians' view rested on the match in coastlines: Reyna must have copied. Details found on no earlier chart could not have been copied, so the new analysis undercuts that view. The blank restates it.

B.why: New details suggest Reyna had some source beyond the old charts. They don't prove he surveyed every inlet himself, which is the extra step this choice requires.

C.why: This is the new finding itself, so it can't be the idea being doubted. You picked the evidence instead of the old view it overturns.

D.why: The analysis is about where Reyna's map came from, not whether the older charts were accurate. Nothing in the passage questions them.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Forecasters have long believed that the summer afternoon thunderstorms in Colter Valley are triggered by moist air drifting up from nearby Lake Annis. But weather-balloon records from several summers when drought had left the lake nearly empty show that storms formed over the valley just as often as in wetter years, casting doubt on the idea that ______
choices: Lake Annis has been nearly empty for most recent summers.
moisture from Lake Annis is what sets off the valley's storms.
the valley's storms are set off by a different moisture source.
thunderstorms rarely form over the valley in drought summers.
explanation: The forecasters' view is that the lake's moisture triggers the storms. If storms formed just as often while the lake was nearly empty, the lake can't be what sets them off. The blank restates that old belief.

A.why: The passage mentions only "several summers" of drought. It never says the lake was low in most recent summers, so this inflates the evidence.

C.why: The balloon data rule out the lake but never identify another moisture source. This is a new claim the study didn't test, not the old view being doubted.

D.why: The records show storms formed in drought summers just as often as in wet ones. This choice reverses what the passage says.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Music historians long believed that composer Anna Lindqvist wrote her six string quartets in the 1790s, since the title page of the manuscript bears the date 1794. However, a recent analysis of the watermarks in the manuscript paper showed that the paper itself was not manufactured until after 1805, casting doubt on the idea that ______
choices: Lindqvist composed the quartets during the 1790s.
Lindqvist wrote the quartets on paper made after 1805.
Lindqvist never composed any music before the year 1805.
watermarks are an unreliable way to date old manuscripts.
explanation: The old view is that the quartets date from the 1790s, and it rests on the 1794 date on the title page. The watermark evidence shows the paper is newer than 1805, which attacks that exact dating. What is being doubted is the old view, that the quartets were composed in the 1790s.

B.why: You picked what the new evidence supports. The watermark analysis points toward this, so it isn't what's being doubted. You landed on the wrong side of the 'however.'

C.why: The study only dates the paper for these six quartets. It says nothing about any other music Lindqvist may have written before 1805, so this goes far beyond what was tested.

D.why: The passage treats the watermark analysis as strong enough to challenge the old dating. It relies on watermarks, so it doesn't call them into question.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Engineers have long assumed that the cracks in ceramic heat-shield coatings form as the coating cools after it is applied, because the cracks are found only on finished, cooled parts. However, materials scientist Priya Raman used high-speed cameras to film the coating as it was being sprayed and saw cracks appearing while the material was still hot, casting doubt on the idea that ______
choices: cracks in the coating begin forming only as it cools.
cracks can appear while the coating is still being sprayed.
the coating cannot be applied to a part without cracking.
high-speed cameras are unable to record cracks as they form.
explanation: The old assumption is that cracks form during cooling. Raman's footage shows cracks forming while the coating is still hot, which directly contradicts that assumption. The idea being doubted is the old view: cracks begin only as the coating cools.

B.why: You picked what Raman's footage actually showed. The new evidence supports this claim, so it can't be the idea being doubted. You landed on the wrong side of the 'however.'

C.why: The study only showed when the cracks form. It never tested whether a crack-free coating is possible, so this claim is much stronger than anything in the passage.

D.why: The passage says the cameras did capture cracks as they appeared. This choice reverses what the text states.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: When childhood asthma visits to clinics in the town of Westbury fell by a fifth after a 2019 smoke-free law took effect in restaurants, local officials credited the law. However, public health researchers found that a neighboring town with no such law saw the same drop in asthma visits over the same period, casting doubt on the idea that ______
choices: the restaurant law caused the drop in Westbury's asthma visits.
asthma visits fell in both towns over the same period of time.
smoke-free laws have no effect on the health of any children.
Westbury's asthma visits did not actually decline after 2019.
explanation: The officials' view is that the law caused the drop, and their only reason is that the drop came after the law. An identical drop in a town without the law weakens that reasoning. So the idea being doubted is that the law caused the decline.

B.why: This is the researchers' new finding, so it can't be what's being doubted. You picked the evidence when the blank asks for the old view it challenges.

C.why: The study looked at one law in two towns. It raises doubt about one claim of cause, but it can't show that smoke-free laws never help any child anywhere.

D.why: Nobody disputes that the visits fell. The passage says they fell by a fifth, and the question is only about why.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Some seismologists have proposed that swarms of small tremors along the Kessler Fault reliably warn of a major earthquake, since such swarms were recorded shortly before the fault's two largest quakes. However, a review of thirty years of monitoring data found dozens of similar swarms that were followed by no large earthquake at all, casting doubt on the idea that ______
choices: tremor swarms on the fault reliably signal a coming major quake.
many tremor swarms on the fault were not followed by a large quake.
tremors on the fault have no connection to its large earthquakes.
the fault's monitoring records were too incomplete to be reviewed.
explanation: The old proposal is that swarms reliably come before major quakes, based on two cases. Dozens of swarms with no quake afterward attack the word 'reliably.' So the idea being doubted is that swarms dependably signal a major quake.

B.why: This restates what the review found. The new evidence supports it, so you chose the wrong side of the 'however.'

C.why: Swarms did come before the two largest quakes, so some connection may still exist. The review shows only that swarms aren't a reliable warning. It doesn't show they have nothing to do with large quakes.

D.why: The passage says thirty years of data were reviewed and produced a clear result. Saying the records couldn't be reviewed contradicts that.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Bridge engineers have long assumed that the steel cables of suspension bridges corrode mainly at their lower anchors, where rainwater tends to collect. However, when inspectors cut apart the cables of a retired bridge in Ohio, they found the heaviest corrosion near the tops of the towers, where the cables pass over metal saddles, casting doubt on the idea that ______
choices: cable corrosion is concentrated mainly at the lower anchors.
the cables corrode most heavily near the tops of the towers.
rainwater plays no part in the corrosion of bridge cables.
the retired bridge's cables showed little corrosion overall.
explanation: The old assumption is that corrosion is worst at the lower anchors. The inspection found the worst corrosion at the top instead, which directly challenges where engineers expected it. The idea being doubted is that corrosion is concentrated at the lower anchors.

B.why: This is what the inspectors found, so the new evidence supports it. You attached your answer to the wrong side of the 'however.'

C.why: The inspection only shows where corrosion was heaviest on one bridge. It never tested whether rainwater matters at all, so this goes beyond the evidence.

D.why: The passage says inspectors found heavy corrosion near the tops of the towers. This choice contradicts that.
